sentences.en: In 2011, the body of a woman was discovered in a California vineyard.
sentences.zh: 2011年，一名女性的遗体在加利福尼亚州的一个葡萄园中被发现。

sentences.en: She had been decapitated, and her body had been drained of blood.
sentences.zh: 她遭到了斩首，体内的血液也被排干。

sentences.en: It appeared her killer had gone to extraordinary lengths to conceal her identity.
sentences.zh: 凶手似乎费尽心机地想要隐瞒她的身份。

sentences.en: For more than a decade, she was known only as Jane Doe.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，她一直被称为“简·多伊”（无名氏）。

sentences.en: Then, detectives finally learned her name, Ada.
sentences.zh: 直到后来，侦探们终于查明了她的名字：艾达。

sentences.en: But identifying her only made this bizarre murder even more perplexing.
sentences.zh: 但确认她的身份反而让这起离奇的谋杀案变得更加扑朔迷离。

sentences.en: Ada is the new series from Casefile Presents, available now wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 《艾达》是“Casefile Presents”推出的全新系列节目，现已在各大播客平台上线。

sentences.en: Hello, it's Casey here.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是凯西。

sentences.en: Over the past couple of weeks, you might have noticed something a little different here on the Casefile feed.
sentences.zh: 过去几周，你们可能注意到“Casefile”的节目源里出现了一些小小的变化。

sentences.en: I recently had the chance to meet some of our listeners at the Casefile live shows and something kept coming up in conversations that really surprised me.
sentences.zh: 最近我有机会在“Casefile”的现场活动中见到了一些听众，谈话中反复出现的一个话题让我非常惊讶。

sentences.en: A lot of people don't know what Casefile Presents is or that we produce other podcasts in addition to Casefile.
sentences.zh: 很多人并不知道什么是“Casefile Presents”，也不知道除了“Casefile”之外，我们还制作了其他播客节目。

sentences.en: It occurred to me that if someone is a big enough supporter of the show to come to a live event but hasn't heard of Casefile Presents,
sentences.zh: 我意识到，如果一个人是节目的忠实支持者，甚至愿意参加现场活动，却还没听说过“Casefile Presents”，

sentences.en: then clearly we need to do a better job of highlighting the other stories we've put so much work and care into.
sentences.zh: 那么显然，我们需要更好地宣传那些我们倾注了大量心血和关怀的其他故事。

sentences.en: For those who don't know, Casefile Presents is our broader production platform.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不了解的人，我解释一下，“Casefile Presents”是我们更广泛的制作平台。

sentences.en: While Casefile is our flagship show, we've also created a number of other podcasts under the Casefile Presents banner.
sentences.zh: 虽然“Casefile”是我们的旗舰节目，但我们在“Casefile Presents”旗下也创作了许多其他播客。

sentences.en: Our level of involvement differs from project to project, but we've played a direct role in all of them, whether that's financing, research, editing, music, or production.
sentences.zh: 我们对每个项目的参与程度各不相同，但无论是在资金、研究、剪辑、音乐还是制作方面，我们都直接参与其中。

sentences.en: I even narrate a few myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己甚至还担任了其中几档节目的旁白。

sentences.en: With Casefile currently on a short break, we felt this was the perfect opportunity to bring some of those other stories into the spotlight.
sentences.zh: 趁着“Casefile”目前处于短暂的休整期，我们觉得这是一个绝佳的机会，可以将那些故事推向台前。

sentences.en: Series that may have slipped under the radar for many of you, but that we've poured a great deal of time, care, and energy into.
sentences.zh: 这些系列节目可能没能引起你们许多人的注意，但我们确实在其中投入了大量的时间、精力和关怀。

sentences.en: We started with Missing Neum, followed by The Bakersfield 3.
sentences.zh: 我们先是推出了《寻找纽姆》，接着是《贝克斯菲尔德三人组》。

sentences.en: And now we're turning our attention to the Frankston murders.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们将目光转向了“弗兰克斯顿连环谋杀案”。

sentences.en: You might remember this case from episode 23 of Casefile, which we released way back in June 2016.
sentences.zh: 你们可能还记得“Casefile”第23期的案件，那是在2016年6月发布的。

sentences.en: It ran for just over an hour and was split across two parts.
sentences.zh: 那期节目时长刚过一小时，分为上下两集。

sentences.en: Those were very early days for the show, when our episodes were shorter, the production was much more basic and our format was still evolving.
sentences.zh: 那时节目还处于起步阶段，集数较短，制作也比较基础，节目形式还在不断演变中。

sentences.en: A few years after that original episode aired, I met Vicky Petratus
sentences.zh: 在那期节目播出几年后，我结识了维基·佩特拉蒂斯。

sentences.en: Vicky is an author who had written a book on the Frankston murders and was living in the area as the crimes were happening
sentences.zh: 维基是一位作家，她曾写过一本关于弗兰克斯顿谋杀案的书，而且在案发时就住在当地。

sentences.en: Over time, she came to know many of the victims' loved ones personally
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，她与许多受害者的亲属建立了私人交情。

sentences.en: Vicky is one of the hardest working people I know She somehow manages to juggle multiple in-depth projects while balancing everything else life throws her way
sentences.zh: 维基是我认识的最勤奋的人之一。她总能同时处理多个深度项目，并兼顾生活中其他琐事。

sentences.en: She has spent decades giving voices to victims and their families And she brings both compassion and commitment to honouring victims
sentences.zh: 几十年来，她一直致力于为受害者及其家属发声。她带着同情心和使命感，通过详尽且尊重的叙述来缅怀受害者。

sentences.en: Through detailed, respectful storytelling
sentences.zh: 通过详尽、尊重的叙事方式。

sentences.en: I knew right away that she was exactly the type of person I wanted to collaborate with on Case File Presents projects
sentences.zh: 我立刻意识到，她正是我想在“Casefile Presents”项目中合作的那类人。

sentences.en: We first worked together on other podcast series But then we found out that Paul Dania
sentences.zh: 我们最初在其他播客系列中合作过。但后来我们得知，保罗·丹尼尔——

sentences.en: The man convicted for the Frankston serial murders had applied for parole.
sentences.zh: 那个因弗兰克斯顿连环谋杀案被定罪的男人，已经申请了假释。

sentences.en: While I was mind-boggled to know that a serial killer could apply for parole, this news triggered many unwelcome feelings for the victim's families.
sentences.zh: 虽然我无法想象连环杀手竟然也能申请假释，但这个消息给受害者家属带来了许多痛苦的回忆。

sentences.en: In addition to fear, it placed a huge emotional burden on them.
sentences.zh: 除了恐惧，这还给他们造成了巨大的心理负担。

sentences.en: There were submissions, paperwork, legal processes, having to relive the worst days of their lives just to keep a serial killer from being released.
sentences.zh: 为了阻止连环杀手获释，他们不得不面对各种申请、文书工作和法律程序，被迫重温人生中最黑暗的日子。

sentences.en: Vicky and I both strongly felt that The Frankston Case deserved a more in-depth series, something that went beyond the headlines to explore the full impact of Danya's crimes.
sentences.zh: 维基和我都强烈地认为，弗兰克斯顿案值得制作一个更深入的系列，去超越新闻头条，探讨丹尼尔罪行带来的全面影响。

sentences.en: In March 2023, we released a brand new 11-part series titled The Frankston Murders.
sentences.zh: 2023年3月，我们发布了一个全新的11集系列节目，名为《弗兰克斯顿谋杀案》。

sentences.en: The series details the lead-up to the crimes as well as the aftermath, the families, the survivors, and the many women who were targeted in the lead-up to the murders
sentences.zh: 该系列详细讲述了案发前后的经过，包括受害者家属、幸存者，以及许多在谋杀案发生前就已成为目标，

sentences.en: but whose stories hadn't yet been told.
sentences.zh: 但她们的故事却从未被讲述过的女性。

sentences.en: The response was incredible.
sentences.zh: 反响非常热烈。

sentences.en: The series went to number one and has been downloaded more than three million times to date.
sentences.zh: 该系列登上了榜首，迄今为止下载量已超过三百万次。

sentences.en: If you missed it the first time round, now is the perfect time to give it a listen.
sentences.zh: 如果你第一次错过的话，现在正是收听的最佳时机。

sentences.en: We're releasing episode one here on the Casefile feed.
sentences.zh: 我们正在“Casefile”的节目源中发布第一集。

sentences.en: If you like what you hear, you can find the rest of the series by searching The Frankston Murders wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个节目，可以在各大播客平台搜索《弗兰克斯顿谋杀案》收听后续内容。

sentences.en: Now, here is episode one.
sentences.zh: 现在，请收听第一集。

sentences.en: My podcast, Casefile True Crime, covered the Frankston serial murders in a two-part episode on Case 23 back in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我的播客“Casefile True Crime”曾在2016年的第23期节目中，分两集报道过弗兰克斯顿连环谋杀案。

sentences.en: When we asked true crime author
sentences.zh: 当我们邀请真实犯罪作家

sentences.en: Vicky Petratis to make a Casefile Presents series on the disappearance of Sarah McDermott from the
sentences.zh: 维基·佩特拉蒂斯为“Casefile Presents”制作一个关于1990年莎拉·麦克德莫特从

sentences.en: Cananooga Railway Station in 1990, it was a natural progression for her to move on to the
sentences.zh: 卡纳努拉火车站失踪的系列节目时，她顺理成章地将下一个播客系列转向了

sentences.en: Frankston murders of 1993 for her next podcast series.
sentences.zh: 1993年的弗兰克斯顿谋杀案。

sentences.en: It was especially timely since serial killer Paul Denyer's 30-year non-parole period on his life sentence was up in mid-2023 and there was a likelihood he would apply for parole.
sentences.zh: 这非常及时，因为连环杀手保罗·丹尼尔终身监禁的30年不得假释期将在2023年中期结束，他很有可能会申请假释。

sentences.en: Vicky wrote the book on the Frankston murders and the case has remained close to her heart.
sentences.zh: 维基写过关于弗兰克斯顿谋杀案的书，这个案件一直让她挂心。

sentences.en: On Friday the 11th of June 1993, 18-year-old
sentences.zh: 1993年6月11日星期五，18岁的

sentences.en: Elizabeth Stevens caught a bus from Frankston to the home she shared with her aunt and uncle in Lang Warren.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·史蒂文斯从弗兰克斯顿乘巴士前往她与姨妈姨父在朗沃伦合住的家中。

sentences.en: She never made it home.
sentences.zh: 但她再也没能到家。

sentences.en: Her body was discovered the following day in Lloyd Park.
sentences.zh: 第二天，她的遗体在劳埃德公园被发现。

sentences.en: On Thursday the 8th of July, 22-year-old Debbie Freem, the mother of a baby boy just 12 days old, was abducted during a trip to her local milk bar to buy milk.
sentences.zh: 7月8日星期四，22岁的黛比·弗里姆，一位刚生下12天大男婴的母亲，在去当地奶吧买奶的途中被绑架。

sentences.en: And finally, on Friday the 30th of July, 17-year-old Natalie Russell didn't make it home from school.
sentences.zh: 最后，在7月30日星期五，17岁的娜塔莉·拉塞尔没能从学校回家。

sentences.en: She was taken in broad daylight by an increasingly reckless killer.
sentences.zh: 她在光天化日之下被一名日益猖狂的凶手带走。

sentences.en: Her parents were able to take a small comfort from the fact that evidence found at her crime scene ensured the serial killer was taken into custody the following day.
sentences.zh: 她的父母从案发现场发现的证据中得到了一丝慰藉，这些证据确保了连环杀手在次日被捕。

sentences.en: An important note, in the past, the Frankston serial killer has identified as female.
sentences.zh: 一个重要的说明：过去，弗兰克斯顿连环杀手曾被认定为女性。

sentences.en: We have it from several sources that this is no longer the case, so we'll use the male name and pronoun.
sentences.zh: 我们从多个渠道获悉事实并非如此，因此我们将使用男性的名字和代词。

sentences.en: We hope that the Frankston Murders podcast will do its bit to bring public awareness to the case, especially as the 30-year non-parole part of Denya's sentence ends in 2023.
sentences.zh: 我们希望《弗兰克斯顿谋杀案》播客能尽一份力，提高公众对该案的关注，特别是在丹尼尔30年不得假释期于2023年结束之际。

sentences.en: He has already applied for parole
sentences.zh: 他已经申请了假释。

sentences.en: In telling this story, we want to keep a serial killer in jail for life He should never be allowed to do to anyone else what he did to people in this podcast
sentences.zh: 在讲述这个故事时，我们希望让连环杀手终身监禁。他不应该再有机会对任何人做出他在本播客中所做过的事情。

sentences.en: We are grateful to the Victoria Police for granting us access to two serving members
sentences.zh: 我们感谢维多利亚州警方允许我们采访两位在职警员，

sentences.en: Leading Senior Constable Angela Bartz and Senior Sergeant Steve Lewis
sentences.zh: 首席高级警员安吉拉·巴茨和高级警长史蒂夫·刘易斯。

sentences.en: All other police members interviewed for this podcast are no longer employed by Victoria Police
sentences.zh: 本播客中采访的所有其他警员均已不再受雇于维多利亚州警方。

sentences.en: We will hand it over to Vicky Petratis to tell the story
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将由维基·佩特拉蒂斯来讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: My name is Vicky Petratis and as a true crime author
sentences.zh: 我叫维基·佩特拉蒂斯，作为一名真实犯罪作家，

sentences.en: I found myself right in the heart of Frankston
sentences.zh: 我发现自己身处弗兰克斯顿的核心地带，

sentences.en: Doing ride-alongs with the local police when the murders were happening
sentences.zh: 在谋杀案发生时，我曾随当地警察一起巡逻。

sentences.en: The seven-week period between June and July 1993 was one Frankston locals will never forget.
sentences.zh: 1993年6月至7月间的七周，是弗兰克斯顿当地人永远无法忘记的时光。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Stevens, Debbie Freem and Natalie Russell all lost their lives at the hand of a serial killer and Rosa Toth came close but luckily escaped.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·史蒂文斯、黛比·弗里姆和娜塔莉·拉塞尔都死于连环杀手之手，罗莎·托特也曾命悬一线，但幸运地逃脱了。

sentences.en: The trail of damage caused by Paul Denier casts a wide net.
sentences.zh: 保罗·丹尼尔造成的破坏轨迹影响深远。

sentences.en: While his victim tally that we know of is three, the ripple effect of what he did is never-ending.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们已知的受害者只有三名，但他所造成的连锁反应是永无止境的。

sentences.en: When I wrote the Frankston Murders book back in 1995,
sentences.zh: 当我在1995年写《弗兰克斯顿谋杀案》这本书时，

sentences.en: I wanted it to be about the girls as much as it was about the killer.
sentences.zh: 我希望它不仅是关于凶手的，更是关于那些女孩的。

sentences.en: To understand the extent of his crimes, we need to know what he took from us.
sentences.zh: 要了解他罪行的严重程度，我们需要知道他从我们这里夺走了什么。

sentences.en: And make no mistake about it,
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，

sentences.en: Paul Denyer ruined more lives than what he took.
sentences.zh: 保罗·丹尼尔毁掉的人生远不止他夺走的那几条生命。

sentences.en: His trail of destruction is wide.
sentences.zh: 他留下的破坏轨迹非常广泛。

sentences.en: When he set out to act on the desires to kill that he'd had since he turned 14, there's no evidence he gave any thought to the heartbreak he would cause.
sentences.zh: 当他开始实施从14岁起就萌生的杀人欲望时，没有任何证据表明他考虑过自己会造成怎样的心碎。

sentences.en: It seemed nothing mattered to him more than his bloodluSt.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，似乎没有什么比他的嗜血更重要了。

sentences.en: I always knew the case would draw me in to revisit it again in podcast form.
sentences.zh: 我一直知道，这个案件最终会吸引我以播客的形式重新审视它。

sentences.en: But perhaps the thing that tipped the scale was a Facebook message I got from a woman called Gloria Vaines.
sentences.zh: 但真正让我下定决心的，或许是我收到的一位名叫格洛丽亚·维恩斯的女性发来的Facebook消息。

sentences.en: It was her daughter, whose cats were killed by Denya.
sentences.zh: 那是她的女儿，她的猫被丹尼尔杀死了。

sentences.en: Four months before the murders began,
sentences.zh: 在谋杀案开始前四个月，

sentences.en: Denya broke into Donna Vaines' house in Claude Street in Seaford and killed her cat and its two kittens.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔闯入了位于西福德克劳德街的唐娜·维恩斯的家，杀死了她的猫和两只小猫。

sentences.en: Gloria told me that Donna never got over it.
sentences.zh: 格洛丽亚告诉我，唐娜一直没能走出阴影。

sentences.en: I put out a call on social media wondering how many other victims were out there.
sentences.zh: 我在社交媒体上发出了呼吁，想看看还有多少受害者。

sentences.en: It wasn't long before a disturbing picture of stalking and attacks on property emerged.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，一幅令人不安的跟踪和财产攻击画面就浮现了出来。

sentences.en: Some stories I'd heard before and others I hadn't.
sentences.zh: 有些故事我以前听说过，有些则没有。

sentences.en: These stories gave me something else to consider.
sentences.zh: 这些故事让我有了新的考量。

sentences.en: There are a lot of women out there who live in fear that Paul Denier might one day be released from jail.
sentences.zh: 有很多女性生活在恐惧中，担心保罗·丹尼尔有一天会被释放出狱。

sentences.en: They're worried he might come after them.
sentences.zh: 她们担心他可能会找上门来。

sentences.en: again.
sentences.zh: 再次找上门来。

sentences.en: In adding these stories to the narrative, the picture that emerges of the warning signs should serve to educate us all.
sentences.zh: 将这些故事加入叙述中，所呈现出的警示信号应该能教育我们所有人。

sentences.en: We don't re-examine this case just to retell the story.
sentences.zh: 我们重新审视这个案件不仅仅是为了重述故事。

sentences.en: We do it so that we can be reminded of just how dangerous Denya was back then and remains so to this day.
sentences.zh: 我们这样做是为了提醒大家，丹尼尔在当时是多么危险，而直到今天依然如此。

sentences.en: And we tell the story so that around the world people can join in the bid to keep him in prison.
sentences.zh: 我们讲述这个故事，是为了让世界各地的人们都能加入到让他继续入狱的呼吁中来。

sentences.en: So many people were affected by the things Paul Denyer did.
sentences.zh: 保罗·丹尼尔所做的一切影响了太多人。

sentences.en: I wanted to begin with a man called Todd, who grew up in Langwarren.
sentences.zh: 我想从一个名叫托德的男人开始讲起，他在朗沃伦长大。

sentences.en: I spoke to Todd at a cafe that he runs a couple of kilometres north of the Melbourne CBD.
sentences.zh: 我在墨尔本中央商务区以北几公里处他经营的一家咖啡馆里采访了托德。

sentences.en: Back in 1992, his family lived in Moat Street, just around the corner from the Denyer family, who then lived in Long Street, a couple of houses down from Todd's kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 1992年，他的家人住在莫特街，就在丹尼尔一家转角处。丹尼尔一家当时住在长街，离托德的幼儿园只有几栋房子的距离。

sentences.en: Our kindergarten had a couple of rabbits in a hutch that was like all the kinder kids looked after, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我们的幼儿园里有一个兔笼，养了几只兔子，我想所有的幼儿园孩子都会照顾它们。

sentences.en: It was in 1992, earlier in 1992, we all came into the kindergarten in the morning.
sentences.zh: 那是1992年，1992年早些时候，我们早上来到幼儿园时。

sentences.en: The rabbits were well and truly dead.
sentences.zh: 那些兔子已经死得透透的了。

sentences.en: They'd been cut up and some of their insides were sort of next to them and it was just sort of left there for all the kinder kids.
sentences.zh: 它们被切开了，内脏散落在旁边，就这样留给所有的幼儿园孩子看。

sentences.en: And obviously the teachers that came in in the morning had all seen it, the kids that had been there had seen it
sentences.zh: 显然，早上来的老师们都看到了，在那里的孩子们也都看到了，

sentences.en: and it spread quite quickly that something pretty awful had happened.
sentences.zh: 这件事很快就传开了，大家都知道发生了非常可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Even though Todd was only a child, he never forgot the killing of the pet rabbits.
sentences.zh: 尽管托德当时只是个孩子，但他从未忘记那些宠物兔被杀的场景。

sentences.en: But it wasn't just the killing of them that was disturbing,
sentences.zh: 但令人不安的不仅仅是杀戮本身，

sentences.en: It was the fact that whoever did it left them for all the children to see.
sentences.zh: 而是做这件事的人竟然把它们留给所有的孩子看。

sentences.en: If you're doing that sort of thing and leaving it at a kindergarten,
sentences.zh: 如果你做这种事并把它留在幼儿园，

sentences.en: you're doing it to cause a reaction.
sentences.zh: 你就是为了引起反应。

sentences.en: It's not out in a paddock or out in the bush where no-one's going to see it.
sentences.zh: 这不是在没人看见的牧场或丛林里。

sentences.en: That is prime where everyone's going to see it and it's probably going to affect people more so.
sentences.zh: 那是每个人都会看到的地方，而且这可能会对人们造成更大的影响。

sentences.en: And I think it was for a shock factor.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是为了制造冲击效果。

sentences.en: It was to scare people.
sentences.zh: 这是为了恐吓人们。

sentences.en: Todd doesn't know for sure whether the police were called to investigate the rabbit killings at the kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 托德不确定警方是否接到报案去调查幼儿园的杀兔事件。

sentences.en: He doesn't remember any police visiting while the children were in attendance.
sentences.zh: 他不记得在孩子们上学期间有警察来过。

sentences.en: The kinder teachers, from what I remember, they took care of it and, look, whether they came after we'd all gone for the day, I'm not sure, but from my knowledge, no.
sentences.zh: 据我记忆，幼儿园老师处理了这件事。至于我们走后他们是否来过，我不确定，但据我所知，没有。

sentences.en: We were fortunate to get well-known forensic psychologist
sentences.zh: 我们很荣幸请到了著名的法医心理学家

sentences.en: Tim Watson-Munro to offer insights into Denya's behaviour.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·沃森-芒罗，为丹尼尔的行为提供见解。

sentences.en: While Tim didn't assess Denya, he has over 40 years' experience of assessing tens of thousands of criminals.
sentences.zh: 虽然蒂姆没有评估过丹尼尔，但他拥有40多年评估数万名罪犯的经验。

sentences.en: We will call on Tim's expertise throughout this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们将在整个播客中借助蒂姆的专业知识。

sentences.en: Where's the empathy?
sentences.zh: 同理心在哪里？

sentences.en: Where's the remorse?
sentences.zh: 悔恨在哪里？

sentences.en: Much the contrary, they're getting a thrill out of it, maybe even watching it from a distance to see what the reaction is.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，他们从中获得了快感，甚至可能在远处观看，看看会有什么反应。

sentences.en: and it's all about power, control, creating fear.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了权力、控制和制造恐惧。

sentences.en: And there are few more effective ways to create fear than killing animals at a kindergarten and leaving them out for the kids to see.
sentences.zh: 而在幼儿园杀死动物并留给孩子们看，是制造恐惧最有效的方法之一。

sentences.en: Two other things stand out in Todd's mind.
sentences.zh: 还有两件事在托德的脑海中记忆犹新。

sentences.en: First, there was an incident one night in his street with a local woman who lived on her own.
sentences.zh: 首先，有一天晚上他住的那条街上发生了一起事件，涉及一位独居的当地女性。

sentences.en: There is no evidence what Todd is about to tell us was Paul Denyer, but a woman was terrorised in her house at night, getting all of the neighbours out of their homes
sentences.zh: 没有证据表明托德接下来要告诉我们的是保罗·丹尼尔所为，但当时一位女性在晚上被困在自己家中，迫使所有邻居都走出家门，

sentences.en: to come to her aid, creating fear.
sentences.zh: 前来援助她，这制造了恐慌。

sentences.en: His involvement can't be discounted.
sentences.zh: 不能排除他的参与。

sentences.en: There was a neighbour of ours that had someone banging on their doors and windows late at night trying to get in and was making a concerted effort to get in.
sentences.zh: 我们的一位邻居深夜有人在敲打他们的门窗，试图闯入，而且是蓄意闯入。

sentences.en: So he's banging on doors, windows, making a scene, getting in somewhere.
sentences.zh: 所以他在敲门、敲窗，制造骚乱，试图进入某个地方。

sentences.en: Well, that was certainly to make an impact, certainly so people would know, but certainly to get something out of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这当然是为了制造影响，当然是为了让人知道，但肯定也是为了从中得到什么。

sentences.en: And the other thing that stands out to Todd was that his parents were quite strict about not letting their kids leave Moat Street on their bikes.
sentences.zh: 另一件让托德印象深刻的事是，他的父母非常严格，不准孩子们骑自行车离开莫特街。

sentences.en: Pushing at this boundary,
sentences.zh: 为了挑战这个界限，

sentences.en: Todd used to ride his bike across the road at the end of his street and go to the service station on Long Street.
sentences.zh: 托德过去常骑车穿过街道尽头的马路，去长街上的加油站。

sentences.en: He and his brothers figured it was safe.
sentences.zh: 他和他的兄弟们觉得那里很安全。

sentences.en: The owners were hard-working people.
sentences.zh: 店主是勤劳的人。

sentences.en: It seemed like a mistake when they employed a young man called Paul to work there.
sentences.zh: 当他们雇佣一个叫保罗的年轻人去那里工作时，似乎是个错误。

sentences.en: Unlike the industrious owners, Paul seemed to stand around and not do much.
sentences.zh: 与勤奋的店主不同，保罗似乎总是游手好闲，什么也不做。

sentences.en: From what I recall, he was a very nondescript person.
sentences.zh: 据我回忆，他是一个非常平庸的人。

sentences.en: There was nothing that stood out about him.
sentences.zh: 他身上没有什么引人注目的地方。

sentences.en: If you passed him on the street, you wouldn't remember him five minutes later.
sentences.zh: 如果你在街上和他擦肩而过，五分钟后你根本不会记得他长什么样。

sentences.en: Look, given he didn't seem to hold down a job very long, the guys that owned that service station, they worked in it seven days a week, knew everyone's names,
sentences.zh: 听着，鉴于他似乎没法在任何工作岗位上待太久，那家加油站的老板可是每周七天都在那儿干活，他们认识每一个人，

sentences.en: and back then it was driveway service.
sentences.zh: 而且那时候还有车道服务。

sentences.en: They used to fill your car back then.
sentences.zh: 那时候他们会帮你把油加满。

sentences.en: I don't think that someone that didn't really do much and just sort of stood around was really going to last very long with these people.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那种没什么正经事做、只会游手好闲的人，在这些人手下是干不长的。

sentences.en: the day that todd has never forgotten his mum pulled into the service station to get petrol
sentences.zh: 托德（Todd）永远忘不了那天，他妈妈开车进加油站加油，

sentences.en: the owner filled up her tank she paid him and paul looked at her car and said she was good to go
sentences.zh: 老板加满了油，她付了钱，保罗（Paul）看了看她的车，说可以走了，

sentences.en: the guy that owned it had filled the car and he'd gone into the payment and mum's in the car
sentences.zh: 老板加完油后去处理付款了，而妈妈还在车里，

sentences.en: yep we're good to go and paul was actually the one that was like yeah yeah yeah good to go the petrol browser was still attached so she just drove out with it still attached
sentences.zh: 没错，我们可以走了，其实是保罗在那儿说“对对对，可以走了”，结果加油枪还插在车上，所以她就那样直接把车开走了，加油枪还连着呢。

sentences.en: and I mean look whether it was an honest mistake don't know but mum was pretty upset and everyone was at the service station.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你看，这到底是不是无心之失我不知道，但妈妈当时非常生气，加油站里的每个人也都看到了。

sentences.en: Looking back on it now you have to wonder if Paul's actions on the day were deliberate.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，你不得不怀疑保罗当天的行为是否是蓄意的。

sentences.en: Did he look at her car, see the nozzle still attached and tell her to go or is it possible the owner replaced the nozzle back on the bowser when he finished filling her car
sentences.zh: 他是看了她的车，看到加油枪还插着却故意叫她开走，还是说老板在加完油后把枪放回了加油机，

sentences.en: and then Paul put it back in the car just to cause mischief or worse?
sentences.zh: 然后保罗又把它插回车里，只是为了搞恶作剧，或者更糟？

sentences.en: Luckily no petrol was spilt and no stray spark turned an embarrassing inconvenience into chaos.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，没有汽油泄漏，也没有杂散的火花将这起尴尬的意外演变成灾难。

sentences.en: When Paul stopped working at the service station, he got a job at Safeway Keringal Hub.
sentences.zh: 保罗从加油站离职后，在凯林加尔中心（Keringal Hub）的赛夫威（Safeway）超市找了份工作。

sentences.en: A story that I heard back when I was writing the book was that Paul Denya had been fired from a supermarket for ramming a woman with some shopping trolleys.
sentences.zh: 我在写书时听到的一个故事是，保罗·德尼耶（Paul Denyer）曾因为用购物车撞了一名妇女而被超市开除。

sentences.en: I didn't know any more details than that.
sentences.zh: 我当时只知道这些，没有更多细节。

sentences.en: A woman called Kate got in touch with me.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫凯特（Kate）的女士联系了我。

sentences.en: It was her mother, Denya, rammed, and she was there and saw it happen.
sentences.zh: 被撞的是她母亲德尼耶（Denya），她当时就在现场，亲眼目睹了经过。

sentences.en: While her mother has since passed away,
sentences.zh: 虽然她母亲后来已经去世了，

sentences.en: Kate never forgot the incident.
sentences.zh: 但凯特从未忘记那次事件。

sentences.en: I was five at the time and my brother he would have been three and my mum at the time was
sentences.zh: 我当时五岁，我弟弟大概三岁，我妈妈当时还

sentences.en: pregnant with my second brother and we used to always shop at Kringle Hub and on this particular
sentences.zh: 怀着我的第二个弟弟。我们以前总是在凯林加尔中心购物，就在那一天，

sentences.en: day my mum had packed my brother and I in the car we had gone shopping and we were getting out of
sentences.zh: 妈妈把我和弟弟安顿在车里，我们去购物，正准备下车，

sentences.en: the car and I could see because I had we got told to stand at the boot and wait for mum there was a guy in the distance collecting trolleys.
sentences.zh: 我能看到，因为我们被告知要站在后备箱旁等妈妈，远处有个家伙在收购物车。

sentences.en: As my mum, my brother and I started to walk towards the entrance to the supermarket, we could see a guy hurrying with the trolleys and he collided with my mum.
sentences.zh: 当我和妈妈、弟弟开始走向超市入口时，我们看到那个家伙推着购物车匆匆赶来，然后撞上了我妈妈。

sentences.en: Kate remembers a slight incline in the car park, but if the man had have accidentally lost control of the trolleys, he made no attempt to warn them.
sentences.zh: 凯特记得停车场有个小斜坡，但如果那人是不小心失去了对购物车的控制，他完全没有试图提醒他们。

sentences.en: He didn't say anything.
sentences.zh: 他什么也没说。

sentences.en: I don't recall him saying get out of the way or excuse me or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我不记得他说过“让开”或“借过”之类的话。

sentences.en: It was just push.
sentences.zh: 他就是直接撞了过来。

sentences.en: There was no one else around and the collision was deliberate.
sentences.zh: 周围没有其他人，那次碰撞是蓄意的。

sentences.en: Kate remembers her pregnant mother being pushed roughly forward with the impact.
sentences.zh: 凯特记得她怀孕的母亲在撞击下被粗暴地向前推去。

sentences.en: The trolleys hit her from behind so she didn't actually see anything but she did actually turn around when the hit happened.
sentences.zh: 购物车从背后撞上她，所以她其实什么也没看见，但在撞击发生时她确实转过了身。

sentences.en: It hit her in the back and so we did quickly move.
sentences.zh: 它撞到了她的后背，所以我们赶紧躲开了。

sentences.en: Kate remembers her mum telling off the man with the trolleys for ramming her.
sentences.zh: 凯特记得她妈妈斥责那个推购物车的男人撞了她。

sentences.en: I asked her whether the man said anything back.
sentences.zh: 我问她那个男人有没有回嘴。

sentences.en: It was just the death stare, he didn't say anything but he sort of just looked in disgust really, just a look of disgust and that icy cold death stare.
sentences.zh: 他只是死死地盯着她，什么也没说，但他表现出一种厌恶，真的，就是那种厌恶的眼神，还有那种冰冷刺骨的死亡凝视。

sentences.en: It was just a look of hatred and I haven't really seen that in people ever like since then but yeah it's a look I've never forgotten.
sentences.zh: 那是一种仇恨的眼神，从那以后我再也没在别人身上见过，真的，那是我永远无法忘记的眼神。

sentences.en: What I'm always interested in is the effect on women of their encounters with Denya.
sentences.zh: 我一直很感兴趣的是，女性在与德尼耶遭遇后会受到什么影响。

sentences.en: She was very shaken up I remember like she just was rattled from the whole experience because I don't think many of us have had that type of
sentences.zh: 她当时非常震惊，我记得她被整个经历吓坏了，因为我觉得我们大多数人都没有过那种

sentences.en: experience and if we have we may have felt a bit of resolve because the person may be a bit remorseful
sentences.zh: 经历，即使有过，我们可能也会感到一丝释然，因为对方可能会感到愧疚

sentences.en: and really apologetic most people are if they've run into someone by accident but this was different
sentences.zh: 并且真心道歉，大多数人如果是不小心撞到人都会这样，但这完全不同。

sentences.en: This was sort of a situation that she'd never encountered before.
sentences.zh: 这是一种她从未遇到过的情况。

sentences.en: I haven't to this day ever encountered something like that since.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我再也没有遇到过类似的事情。

sentences.en: And it did rattle her.
sentences.zh: 这确实让她感到不安。

sentences.en: She changed the way we used to shop.
sentences.zh: 她改变了我们购物的方式。

sentences.en: We used to shop Keringle, then she used to shop elsewhere because of that whole entire experience.
sentences.zh: 我们以前常去凯林加尔购物，后来因为那次经历，她就去别的地方买了。

sentences.en: And in this brief but significant encounter, what does Kate feel about the violence and the hatred emanating from the man in the Safeway car park.
sentences.zh: 在这次短暂但意义重大的遭遇中，凯特对那个在赛夫威停车场散发出暴力和仇恨的男人有什么感觉？

sentences.en: When you're not happy with someone, you might see someone with a death stare and they don't blink.
sentences.zh: 当你对某人不满意时，你可能会看到有人用死亡凝视盯着你，他们连眼都不眨。

sentences.en: They just stare straight through you as if you're a pane of glass.
sentences.zh: 他们就这样直勾勾地盯着你，仿佛你是一块玻璃板。

sentences.en: And so I do remember the piercing eyes that were glaring at my brother, my mum and I, but it was just this look of hatred at my mum for some reason.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实记得那双刺眼的眼睛，它们瞪着我弟弟、我和我妈妈，但不知为何，那眼神里充满了对我妈妈的仇恨。

sentences.en: Like, we never knew this person.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们根本不认识这个人。

sentences.en: I'd never seen this person in my life.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子从来没见过这个人。

sentences.en: And if Kate's story wasn't bad enough, I found out that Denya rammed another woman with the supermarket trolleys.
sentences.zh: 如果凯特的故事还不够糟糕的话，我还发现德尼耶曾用超市购物车撞过另一名妇女。

sentences.en: Davin was the assistant manager at the time.
sentences.zh: 达文（Davin）当时是助理经理。

sentences.en: Paul had been at Safeway for around six months and had not even tried to impress his employers.
sentences.zh: 保罗在赛夫威工作了大约六个月，甚至没想过要给雇主留下好印象。

sentences.en: Paul worked under me.
sentences.zh: 保罗在我手下工作。

sentences.en: I really didn't think much of him at all.
sentences.zh: 我对他一点好感都没有。

sentences.en: He wasn't a very good worker.
sentences.zh: 他不是个好员工。

sentences.en: He had a very short temper.
sentences.zh: 他的脾气非常暴躁。

sentences.en: He would be constantly having to go and get a mopping bucket because we were just putting him in the drink aisle and he'd be breaking stuff and dropping stuff
sentences.zh: 他总是不得不去拿拖把桶，因为我们把他安排在饮料区，他总是弄坏东西、摔东西，

sentences.en: and you'd hear him cursing and swearing and he was really short fuse.
sentences.zh: 你会听到他骂骂咧咧的，他真的很容易发火。

sentences.en: I think he was only there about six months working there part-time.
sentences.zh: 我想他只在那里兼职工作了大约六个月。

sentences.en: I really didn't think much of him at all as an employee.
sentences.zh: 作为员工，我对他真的没什么好印象。

sentences.en: This time when Dania rammed another woman, there was a baby in her trolley.
sentences.zh: 这次德尼耶撞到另一名妇女时，她的购物车里还有一个婴儿。

sentences.en: On the day that he ran the woman and the child with the row of shopping trolls, I was actually standing there when he did it.
sentences.zh: 在他用一排购物车撞倒那个妇女和孩子的那天，我其实就站在旁边。

sentences.en: I actually saw him do it.
sentences.zh: 我亲眼看见他干的。

sentences.en: He just, the look on his face just went straight into him.
sentences.zh: 他就是……他脸上的表情直接冲着他们去了。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, oh, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, and started apologising.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，哦，对不起，对不起，开始道歉了。

sentences.en: I don't know whether he intended to hit him as hard as he did, but he did knock the woman over, the trolley over, the baby out of the trolley.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他是不是故意撞得那么重，但他确实把那个妇女撞倒了，购物车翻了，婴儿也从车里摔了出来。

sentences.en: So we ended up taking him down to the doctors across the road, the medical centre.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最后把他带到了马路对面的医生那里，就是那个医疗中心。

sentences.en: The woman and the baby were taken to the hospital for observation.
sentences.zh: 那个妇女和婴儿被送往医院观察。

sentences.en: For the managers at Safeway, it was the last straw as far as Paul Denyer was concerned.
sentences.zh: 对于赛夫威的经理们来说，就保罗·德尼耶而言，这是压死骆驼的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: The manager called me in because I'd told him what I'd seen.
sentences.zh: 经理把我叫了进去，因为我告诉了他我所看到的一切。

sentences.en: He goes, right, we're going to sack him.
sentences.zh: 他说，好了，我们要解雇他。

sentences.en: You're with me?
sentences.zh: 你跟我一起吗？

sentences.en: You're going to back me?
sentences.zh: 你会支持我吗？

sentences.en: I'm like, yep, no worries at all.
sentences.zh: 我说，没问题，完全没问题。

sentences.en: So we got him in.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把他叫了进来。

sentences.en: He seemed to be quite calm.
sentences.zh: 他看起来相当冷静。

sentences.en: We just explained the situation.
sentences.zh: 我们只是解释了情况。

sentences.en: This woman's had to be taken to the doctors and the baby's taken to the doctors and it looks like they're both going to end up in hospital for observation.
sentences.zh: 这个妇女不得不去看医生，婴儿也看了医生，看起来他们两个都要住院观察。

sentences.en: and, yeah, we were happy to get rid of him, I think, because he was such a bad employee.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，我们很高兴能摆脱他，我想，因为他是个糟糕透顶的员工。

sentences.en: It was at the Karingal Hub Safeway that Paul met Sharon Johnson and the two began dating.
sentences.zh: 正是在凯林加尔中心的赛夫威，保罗遇到了莎伦·约翰逊（Sharon Johnson），两人开始约会。

sentences.en: She was 17 at the time and he was 19.
sentences.zh: 她当时17岁，他19岁。

sentences.en: Five months later, Paul moved into Sharon's mother's house.
sentences.zh: 五个月后，保罗搬进了莎伦母亲的家里。

sentences.en: A month later, Paul and Sharon moved into a unit on the Frankston-Dandenong Road.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，保罗和莎伦搬进了弗兰克斯顿-丹德农路（Frankston-Dandenong Road）的一套公寓。

sentences.en: In the same block of units lived a woman called Julia.
sentences.zh: 在同一栋公寓楼里住着一位名叫朱莉娅（Julia）的女士。

sentences.en: She'd lived there for about a year when Paul Denyer and his girlfriend Sharon moved into the unit next door in September 1992.
sentences.zh: 1992年9月，当保罗·德尼耶和他的女友莎伦搬进隔壁公寓时，她已经在那里住了大约一年了。

sentences.en: I moved into the second unit.
sentences.zh: 我搬进了第二套公寓。

sentences.en: There were four units and they numbered one to four from the road backwards.
sentences.zh: 那里有四套公寓，从路边往里数编号是一到四。

sentences.en: And I moved in the end of 1990, just before I went to uni.
sentences.zh: 我在1990年底搬进去的，就在我去上大学之前。

sentences.en: and about a year later, Paul and Sharon moved in next door into Unit 1.
sentences.zh: 大约一年后，保罗和莎伦搬进了隔壁的1号公寓。

sentences.en: Tricia lived in Unit 3 and there were other people in Unit 4, but I don't recall their names.
sentences.zh: 翠西娅（Tricia）住在3号公寓，4号公寓里还有其他人，但我记不起他们的名字了。

sentences.en: It wasn't long before Paul began calling into Julia's for coffee.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，保罗就开始到朱莉娅家喝咖啡。

sentences.en: During these visits, he would pour his heart out.
sentences.zh: 在这些拜访中，他会倾诉心声。

sentences.en: He was grappling with aspects of his religion.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在纠结自己宗教信仰的某些方面。

sentences.en: When he began dating Sharon, he started going with her to the Christian church on the corner of Madden Street and Frankston-Dannenong Road.
sentences.zh: 当他开始和莎伦约会时，他开始陪她去马登街（Madden Street）和弗兰克斯顿-丹德农路拐角处的基督教堂。

sentences.en: Paul told Julia the church didn't approve of he and Sharon living together, and that angered him.
sentences.zh: 保罗告诉朱莉娅，教会不赞成他和莎伦同居，这让他很生气。

sentences.en: Julia listened to his concerns and offered advice where she could.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅倾听了他的烦恼，并尽可能地提供建议。

sentences.en: Certainly he was a man with issues, and certainly he was upset and asking some big questions and just trying to wrestle through,
sentences.zh: 他确实是个有很多问题的人，也确实很苦恼，提出了一些重大的问题，只是试图挣扎着去理清，

sentences.en: I guess, a fight with what he wanted, what he felt other people approved of or didn't approve of and feeling unhappy about the interactions that he'd had
sentences.zh: 我想，他在与自己想要的、与他觉得别人赞成或不赞成的事情做斗争，并对他们一直去的教会的互动感到不开心，

sentences.en: with the church that they had been going to.
sentences.zh: 他所经历的那些互动。

sentences.en: And I think he was just processing that and trying to move through it.
sentences.zh: 我想他只是在消化这些，并试图走出来。

sentences.en: And certainly I just put that all down to his bucket of issues.
sentences.zh: 我当然把这一切都归结为他那一堆问题。

sentences.en: because paul's partner sharon was working two jobs julia only really saw her in passing
sentences.zh: 因为保罗的伴侣莎伦打两份工，朱莉娅只是偶尔见到她。

sentences.en: it's just very neighborly waving hello maybe a quick chat on the front doorstep i can't recall
sentences.zh: 就是非常邻里间的打个招呼，也许在门口简单聊两句，我不记得她进来喝过咖啡，但如果她愿意，我非常欢迎。

sentences.en: her ever coming in for coffee but she would have been very welcome to do so i tended to see her
sentences.zh: 我通常是在她去上班或下班回家时见到她。

sentences.en: when she was on her way to work or just coming back home from work when paul spoke about attending
sentences.zh: 当保罗谈到去马登街的基督中心参加礼拜时，那离他们的公寓楼大约两分钟车程，朱莉娅记得那个教会和他们家有亲戚关系。

sentences.en: services at the Christian Centre in Madden Street, which was about a two-minute drive away from their block of units, Julia remembers a family connection to the church.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信她的叔叔是那里的牧师，他们去那里有一段时间了，他们决定住在一起，

sentences.en: So I believe her uncle was the pastor there and they had been going there for a while and they had decided to move in together
sentences.zh: 我想教会对他们说，听着，你知道，这可能不是个好主意。

sentences.en: and I think the church had said to them, look, you know, that's probably not the greatest idea.
sentences.zh: 你们要不结婚，要不就别住在一起？

sentences.en: How about you get married or don't live together?
sentences.zh: 保罗对此反应非常消极，这导致了很多质疑和愤怒，也许他觉得他们应该赞成，

sentences.en: Paul had taken that quite poorly and that had resulted in a lot of questioning and some anger that perhaps he felt like they ought to have approved
sentences.zh: 他们应该接受他的决定。

sentences.en: and they ought to have been okay with his decision.
sentences.zh: 我问朱莉娅这是否导致了保罗和莎伦之间的隔阂。

sentences.en: I asked Julia if this caused a division between Paul and Sharon.
sentences.zh: 我心想，如果她的叔叔是牧师，那么他们同居的安排被拒绝会不会让他们更加难受？

sentences.en: I wondered if her uncle was the pastor, then could the rejection of their living arrangements have been doubly difficult?
sentences.zh: 这似乎并没有成为他和莎伦之间的分歧点。

sentences.en: It didn't seem to come up that that was a dividing point between him and Sharon.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们在做决定和想要在一起并住在一起这件事上非常一致。

sentences.en: I think they were quite cohesive in their decision-making and wanting to be together and live next door.
sentences.zh: 我不认为教会介入了他们之间，但我认为也许他失去了一个他曾经参与的社区，他感到有点被排挤了，

sentences.en: And I don't think the church was coming in between them, but I think that perhaps there was a loss of community for him that he had been part of and he felt a bit ousted,
sentences.zh: 我想这对很多人来说都是痛苦的。

sentences.en: which I think would be painful for many people.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅自己也是个有信仰的人，她很乐意和保罗讨论这些事情。

sentences.en: Julia was a person of faith herself and she was happy to discuss these things with Paul.
sentences.zh: 他会出现在她门口，她会煮咖啡，然后他们会聊很久。

sentences.en: He would appear at her door, she would make coffee and then they would talk at length.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会弹吉他。

sentences.en: Sometimes they played the guitar.
sentences.zh: 尽管当时保罗正在跟踪女性并制造武器，但朱莉娅并没有看到他那一面。

sentences.en: And even though it was a time when Paul was stalking women and making weapons, Julia didn't see that side of him.
sentences.zh: 在我们一起喝咖啡的时候，我从来没见过那一面。

sentences.en: I never saw that in the time that we had coffee.
sentences.zh: 他会过来，我们煮咖啡，

sentences.en: He would come over, we would make coffee,
sentences.zh: 我们会坐下来，我有几张沙发。

sentences.en: We'd sit down on the, I had a couple of sofas.
sentences.zh: 他会拿起吉他弹奏，随便拨弄几个和弦，然后聊天。

sentences.en: He would grab the guitar and play the guitar and just kind of mess around with chords and chat.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他认为这是一个安全的空间，可以谈谈他的现状和感受。

sentences.en: I felt like he thought it was a safe space to just kind of talk about where he was at and what he was feeling.
sentences.zh: 鉴于她是在和一个几个月后就要成为连环杀手的人一起喝咖啡，朱莉娅有没有注意到什么迹象？

sentences.en: Given that she was doing coffee with a man who was months away from becoming a serial killer, did Julia notice any signs?
sentences.zh: 我觉得最奇怪的是，什么都没显露出来。

sentences.en: I think what's weirdest is that nothing stood out.
sentences.zh: 没有任何预感。

sentences.en: There wasn't a sense.
sentences.zh: 我没有任何直觉，或者觉得“天哪，你真奇怪”。

sentences.en: I didn't get any spidey sense or my goodness you're weird.
sentences.zh: 我想他确实有很多问题，但我觉得每个人都有自己的问题，我想当我们找到我们认为安全的空间来谈论这些时，我们就会谈论它们，

sentences.en: I think it certainly had a lot of issues but I think everybody has their issues and I think when we find what we think is a safe space to talk about
sentences.zh: 但没有什么让我觉得“哇，你吓到我了”。当然，多年来我见过很多人，特别是在我做护士的角色中，

sentences.en: those that we do talk about them but there wasn't anything where I thought wow you scare me and certainly I've met many people over the years particularly my role as a nurse
sentences.zh: 我见过一些可怕的角色，然而我觉得我见过的最可怕的人之一，可能就是我当时没注意到他很可怕的那个人。

sentences.en: I've met a few scary characters, and yet I think probably one of the scariest people I've ever met is someone I didn't notice was scary at the time.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得他们满身问题。

sentences.en: I just thought they were issue-filled.
sentences.zh: 我和很多认识掠食者的人聊过，他们在知道真相之前也没看出来。

sentences.en: I've spoken to a lot of people who've known predators and didn't pick it before they knew.
sentences.zh: 人们经常会有一种感觉：为什么我没看出来？

sentences.en: There's often a sense of, why didn't I know?
sentences.zh: 我怎么可能没发现？

sentences.en: How could I not have picked it?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，

sentences.en: But the thing is,
sentences.zh: 掠食者是披着羊皮的狼。

sentences.en: Predators are wolves in sheep's clothing.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长隐藏自己的真实本性，欺骗周围的人。

sentences.en: They are very good at hiding their true nature and fooling the people around them.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，朱莉娅有几位住客，所以她那里人来人往。

sentences.en: During this time, Julia had a couple of houseguests, so hers was a place where people were coming and going.
sentences.zh: 当她开始注意到公寓里的东西被动过时，她把它归咎于粗心的住客。

sentences.en: When she began noticing things disturbed around her unit, she put it down to careless houseguests.
sentences.zh: 我会走进屋子，发现东西被稍微移动过。

sentences.en: I would walk into the house and I would find that things had been slightly moved.
sentences.zh: 还有，我在厨房窗台上放了一套水壶和几个杯子，其中一个被撞进了水槽里摔碎了，地板上还有树叶和泥土。

sentences.en: Also that I had a series of like a jug and a number of mugs on the kitchen
sentences.zh: 鉴于我从不使用后门，公寓里不应该有来自后院的树叶和泥土，因为我们根本从不用那扇门。

sentences.en: windowsill and one of them had been knocked into the sink and had broken and there had been leaves and dirt on the floor.
sentences.zh: 而且鉴于我从不使用后门，公寓里不应该有来自后院的树叶和泥土，因为我们根本从不用那扇门。

sentences.en: And given that I never used our back door, there would not have been any of the leaves and dirt from the backyard in the unit because we just never used the door.
sentences.zh: 而且鉴于我从不使用后门，公寓里不应该有来自后院的树叶和泥土，因为我们根本从不用那扇门。

sentences.en: and I found them there and because I'd had people staying with me, I wasn't particularly
sentences.zh: 我在那儿发现了它们，因为我之前有客人住过，所以我并没有特别

sentences.en: concerned.
sentences.zh: 在意。

sentences.en: I just figured these things that happened by accident, clean them up and just put it down to having guests.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这些事情是偶然发生的，清理干净就行了，就把这归咎于有客人来访。

sentences.en: Although I was a little bit surprised that they didn't say, we're sorry for breaking that coffee cup or whatever, but that's okay.
sentences.zh: 虽然我有点惊讶他们没有说“抱歉弄坏了那个咖啡杯”之类的，但那也没关系。

sentences.en: That's just the nature of having guests sometimes.
sentences.zh: 这就是有时接待客人的常态。

sentences.en: And so I put it all down to it being visitors rather than it being an unwelcome visitor.
sentences.zh: 所以我把这一切都归结为是访客所为，而不是什么不受欢迎的入侵者。

sentences.en: But if it had never occurred to Julia that someone had been coming into her unit when she wasn't there, her thinking changed dramatically when she arrived home after a
sentences.zh: 但如果说朱莉娅从未想过有人会在她不在时进入她的公寓，那么在她结束一次

sentences.en: trip to face a disturbing home invasion.
sentences.zh: 旅行回到家，面对一场令人不安的入室行窃后，她的想法发生了剧变。

sentences.en: I'd been away interstate and had come home quite late of an evening and I had had some people staying at my unit.
sentences.zh: 我当时去外州了，晚上很晚才回到家，之前我公寓里住过一些人。

sentences.en: So there were about three people staying at the unit.
sentences.zh: 当时大约有三个人住在公寓里。

sentences.en: And when I got back, I couldn't get inside the unit because they had the chain across the door.
sentences.zh: 当我回来时，我进不去，因为他们把防盗链挂上了。

sentences.en: So I ended up going back to my then fiance's family and staying the night with them and coming back the next day.
sentences.zh: 所以我只好回到当时未婚夫的家里过夜，第二天再回来。

sentences.en: When we entered, I realised that things had been moved.
sentences.zh: 当我们进去时，我意识到东西被动过了。

sentences.en: And when I asked the people who were there why are the things moved or did you move that thing they said oh no
sentences.zh: 当我问那里的人为什么东西被动过，或者是不是你们动了那些东西时，他们说哦不，

sentences.en: it was it was there when we had been coming in and out and it was just different bits and pieces
sentences.zh: 我们进进出出时它就在那儿，只是公寓里的一些零碎物件

sentences.en: around the unit had just changed position and then I started to look at various photos that I
sentences.zh: 改变了位置，然后我开始查看我

sentences.en: had around the unit and in all of the photos there had been a slash in a cross shape across my neck.
sentences.zh: 放在公寓里的各种照片，所有的照片里，我的脖子位置都被划出了十字形的痕迹。

sentences.en: There was a message carved into my piano and there were slash marks across a tall boy.
sentences.zh: 我的钢琴上刻着一条信息，高柜上也留下了划痕。

sentences.en: And the more I looked, the more things I found.
sentences.zh: 我看得越仔细，发现的东西就越多。

sentences.en: I found that my doona had been shredded, that my mattress had been stabbed, that the dress that I had worn to my engagement was slashed through.
sentences.zh: 我发现我的羽绒被被撕碎了，床垫被捅破了，我订婚时穿的那件裙子也被划开了。

sentences.en: and even later going into different drawers in that tall boy, finding passport photos and things stabbed and shredded.
sentences.zh: 甚至后来去翻那个高柜里的不同抽屉，发现护照照片和其他东西也被捅破、撕碎了。

sentences.en: So it just seemed to be this voyage of discovery and then I would find another thing that had been knocked over or smashed or cut through.
sentences.zh: 这似乎成了一场“发现之旅”，我会不断发现又有别的东西被推倒、砸碎或割破。

sentences.en: The more Julia discovered, the more bizarre the break-ins seemed.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅发现的越多，这些入室行窃就显得越离奇。

sentences.en: It was incredibly bizarre and just that I would keep discovering new things and think, oh, well, that's another thing.
sentences.zh: 这简直不可思议，我不断发现新东西，心想，哦，好吧，又是一件。

sentences.en: And I was fairly young at the time.
sentences.zh: 那时候我还很年轻。

sentences.en: I would have been 19 or 20.
sentences.zh: 我大概才19或20岁。

sentences.en: So I was fairly naive.
sentences.zh: 所以我相当天真。

sentences.en: And there was a sense of unreality about,
sentences.zh: 而且有一种不真实感，

sentences.en: I guess, the viciousness and the anti-woman kind of message that it was sending, the slicing through the neck and the shredding of the bedding.
sentences.zh: 我想，那种残忍以及它所传达的某种反女性的信息，比如划破脖子和撕碎寝具。

sentences.en: And I mean, that's all very personal and it's all very, it's really violent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常私人，而且真的非常暴力。

sentences.en: But I wasn't used to that kind of, you know, that was not a characteristic of anything that I'd had experience with before.
sentences.zh: 但我以前没见过那种事，你知道，那不是我以往经历过的任何事情的特征。

sentences.en: So it was very new and it was very unsettling, deeply unsettling.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常新鲜，也非常令人不安，深感不安。

sentences.en: Once she had found out how the intruder had gained access, the point of entry only served to make the break-in more frightening.
sentences.zh: 一旦她发现入侵者是如何进入的，这个入口点只会让这起入室行窃变得更加可怕。

sentences.en: Whoever had entered her unit had been coming in and out for a while.
sentences.zh: 无论谁进入了她的公寓，都已经进进出出好一阵子了。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until later when I discovered that the fly wire in the kitchen had been sliced at the bottom and along each side so that you could just roll the fly wire up
sentences.zh: 直到后来我才发现厨房的纱窗在底部和两侧都被割开了，这样你就可以直接把纱窗卷起来，

sentences.en: and come into the kitchen through the window that it all started to make sense.
sentences.zh: 然后从窗户进入厨房，一切才开始说得通。

sentences.en: and then I realised that probably he had been coming in and out of the unit for a while because when I realised that the photos had been slashed and all of those
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到他可能已经进出公寓好一阵子了，因为当我意识到照片被划破，所有这些

sentences.en: things had occurred, then we started looking more closely at how might someone have gotten in,
sentences.zh: 事情发生时，我们开始更仔细地观察某人是怎么进来的，

sentences.en: what was going on and because it was only really a three or two bedrooms and a living area in a
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么，因为那真的只有两三间卧室、一个起居区和一个

sentences.en: kitchen, they were tiny units, there wasn't much to look at and then all of a sudden it occurred to me, well, hang on a minute, the fly wire's cut.
sentences.zh: 厨房，那是很小的公寓，没什么可看的，突然我想到，等等，纱窗被割开了。

sentences.en: That's how someone's been getting in and out.
sentences.zh: 这就是某人进进出出的方式。

sentences.en: And then that forced me to look back and say, well, okay, that's where the mud on the floor came from
sentences.zh: 这迫使我回想并说，好吧，地板上的泥土就是这么来的，

sentences.en: and the leaves on the floor and how the cup got broken and why things have been moving around my house.
sentences.zh: 还有地板上的树叶，杯子是怎么碎的，以及为什么我屋里的东西会被挪动。

sentences.en: And I haven't really been paying enough attention with that front part of your mind that
sentences.zh: 我之前并没有足够留心，没有用那种

sentences.en: actually has a good hard look at things instead of just brushing it aside and attributing it to something else.
sentences.zh: 真正仔细审视事物的思维去思考，而是直接忽略了，并将其归因于其他原因。

sentences.en: Julia reported the break-in to the police.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅向警方报了案。

sentences.en: They sent out someone sometime later to do fingerprints, but I'm not sure that that netted any great result for them.
sentences.zh: 他们后来派人来提取指纹，但我不太确定这对他们有什么重大结果。

sentences.en: As Julia continued to sort through her unit to assess the extent of the damage the intruder had caused, she found a knife in its box up the top of her wardrobe.
sentences.zh: 当朱莉娅继续整理公寓以评估入侵者造成的破坏程度时，她在衣柜顶部的盒子里发现了一把刀。

sentences.en: It was one of the engagement gifts she had set aside for when she got married.
sentences.zh: 那是她留着结婚时用的订婚礼物之一。

sentences.en: Julia realised this was what the intruder had used to slash her clothes and her bedding.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅意识到这就是入侵者用来划破她衣服和寝具的凶器。

sentences.en: You know the Wiltshire Stay Sharp kind of knives, the really long ones?
sentences.zh: 你知道那种Wiltshire Stay Sharp牌的刀吗，特别长的那种？

sentences.en: We had got one as an engagement present and I realised later that's what he had used.
sentences.zh: 我们收到过一把作为订婚礼物，后来我意识到他就是用了那把刀。

sentences.en: He'd been up in the wardrobe, pulled out the knife and then slashed everything.
sentences.zh: 他爬进衣柜，拿出那把刀，然后把所有东西都划烂了。

sentences.en: So I went back to the police station and said, I think here's your weapon of opportunity, if you like.
sentences.zh: 所以我回到警察局说，我想这就是你们要找的作案工具，如果你们需要的话。

sentences.en: And the response was, well, yeah, okay.
sentences.zh: 他们的反应是，好吧，知道了。

sentences.en: So they added a little bit to the police report and that was that.
sentences.zh: 于是他们在警察报告里加了一点内容，事情就这样了。

sentences.en: Julia told the police she thought it was her neighbour, Paul, who had broken in.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅告诉警察，她认为闯入者是她的邻居保罗。

sentences.en: There were a couple of really good reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 这有几个非常充分的理由。

sentences.en: Her friendship with him had cooled when he began avoiding her and because the intruder had come in through the kitchen window, which was at the back of the units,
sentences.zh: 她和他的友谊在他开始回避她时就变冷了，而且因为入侵者是从厨房窗户进来的，那是在公寓后面，

sentences.en: it meant that access was limited to those living in the block of units.
sentences.zh: 这意味着只有住在这一排公寓里的人才能进入。

sentences.en: Just a feeling that it was Paul next door and I think part of that was because of the access through the back courtyard in that he would be able to gain access.
sentences.zh: 就是一种感觉，觉得是隔壁的保罗，我想部分原因是可以通过后院进入，他有能力进入。

sentences.en: There wasn't a fence between each unit as such.
sentences.zh: 每间公寓之间并没有那种围栏。

sentences.en: And I think because he was probably one of the few people who would have had access to the rear areas of the units to be able to come in through the window.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，因为他可能是少数几个能进入公寓后区并从窗户进来的人之一。

sentences.en: I think at the original report, I was a bit concerned that it may have been Paul, but then when I took the knife into the police station to get them to add it to the report,
sentences.zh: 我想在最初报案时，我有点担心可能是保罗，但后来我把刀带到警察局让他们加进报告时，

sentences.en: And I said, I really think it's my neighbour and this is why.
sentences.zh: 我说，我真的觉得是我的邻居，原因如下。

sentences.en: He was just really unusual when I was leaving and it seemed to be suspicious, his behaviour, and very different to the way that he'd behaved to me before then.
sentences.zh: 我离开时他表现得非常反常，他的行为似乎很可疑，和我之前认识的他完全不同。

sentences.en: Despite the violence of what had happened in her unit,
sentences.zh: 尽管她的公寓里发生了暴力事件，

sentences.en: Julia felt that for the police it was just another break-in.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅觉得对警察来说，这只是又一起普通的入室行窃。

sentences.en: It just seemed to be another break-in report.
sentences.zh: 这看起来就像又一份入室行窃报告。

sentences.en: I guess at the time I thought, well, yeah, there's probably a lot of break-ins that happen and this is probably very run-of-the-mill
sentences.zh: 我想当时我心想，好吧，可能发生了很多入室行窃，这对于警察来说

sentences.en: for police to be processing this kind of complaint.
sentences.zh: 处理这类投诉可能非常司空见惯。

sentences.en: But of course, it wasn't run-of-the-mill.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这并不寻常。

sentences.en: When someone's house is broken into, it's usually for the purpose of robbery.
sentences.zh: 当某人的房子被闯入时，通常是为了抢劫。

sentences.en: But nothing had been stolen.
sentences.zh: 但什么都没丢。

sentences.en: This was an attack.
sentences.zh: 这是一次攻击。

sentences.en: I think now it might be seen in a different light.
sentences.zh: 我想现在可能会以不同的眼光来看待这件事。

sentences.en: We know much more about these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 我们对这类事情了解得多了很多。

sentences.en: I guess even now you're just bringing that up.
sentences.zh: 我想即使是现在，你提起这件事时，

sentences.en: I never thought of it as anything but a break-in.
sentences.zh: 我从未想过它除了入室行窃之外还有别的含义。

sentences.en: Isn't that unusual, I suppose?
sentences.zh: 这难道不奇怪吗，我想？

sentences.en: Because actually he didn't take anything, as far as I know.
sentences.zh: 因为据我所知，他实际上什么都没拿。

sentences.en: Just damaged a lot of things maliciously.
sentences.zh: 只是恶意损坏了很多东西。

sentences.en: And personally, never took a thing.
sentences.zh: 而且针对个人，什么都没拿。

sentences.en: Not really a break-in.
sentences.zh: 这不完全是入室行窃。

sentences.en: With the damage that was done in her unit,
sentences.zh: 看着她公寓里造成的破坏，

sentences.en: Julia could tell it was a personal attack against her.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅能看出这是一次针对她个人的攻击。

sentences.en: But as a young woman, couldn't imagine how or why anyone could hold such a grudge that they would do this to her.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个年轻女性，她无法想象为什么有人会怀有如此深仇大恨，以至于会对她做这种事。

sentences.en: It was a very personal thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常私人的事情。

sentences.en: And then it was like, who hates me?
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是，谁恨我？

sentences.en: Not that I was not, you know, not unlovable, because I think horses for courses, there are people who will love you and there are people who won't love you.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我不可爱，因为我认为萝卜青菜各有所爱，有人会爱你，也有人不会爱你。

sentences.en: It wasn't that I was special, but there was a sense of this very personal thing happening and that it was very personally directed at me
sentences.zh: 并不是我有什么特别，但有一种感觉，这是一件非常私人的事情，而且是专门针对我的，

sentences.en: and I couldn't work out why anyone would put themselves out so much to be so vicious.
sentences.zh: 我无法理解为什么有人会费这么大劲去表现得如此恶毒。

sentences.en: Julia made immediate plans to leave the unit.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅立即计划搬离这间公寓。

sentences.en: After the break-in that was so personal and so inherently violent, it was impossible to stay.
sentences.zh: 在经历了如此私人且本质上如此暴力的入室行窃后，她不可能再住下去了。

sentences.en: I remember calling the landlady and just saying, look, this thing's happened and I need to move out.
sentences.zh: 我记得给房东打电话说，看，发生了这种事，我需要搬走。

sentences.en: and I'm a bit concerned that it may be Paul.
sentences.zh: 而且我有点担心可能是保罗干的。

sentences.en: Paul continued to act oddly right up to the day Julia was packing to leave.
sentences.zh: 直到朱莉娅打包搬走的那天，保罗的行为依然很古怪。

sentences.en: When I was cleaning out my unit,
sentences.zh: 当我清理公寓时，

sentences.en: I had had my aunt there to give me some assistance and she'd left and so it was just me taking out the last few boxes and doing a bit of cleaning and he arrived home
sentences.zh: 我让我的阿姨来帮我，她走后，就剩下我一个人搬走最后几个箱子并做些清理，这时他回家了，

sentences.en: And normally I'd get a wave and a hello and all of those things, but he actually almost raced inside and shut all of the shutters,
sentences.zh: 平时我会得到一个挥手或一声问候，但这次他几乎是冲进屋里，关上了所有的百叶窗，

sentences.en: the front blinds and everything, so that you couldn't see in or out.
sentences.zh: 前窗帘什么的，让你从外面看不见里面，里面也看不见外面。

sentences.en: And that was unusual and that just seemed to be confirming my thoughts that it was him that had done those things.
sentences.zh: 这很不寻常，这似乎证实了我的想法，即这些事情确实是他做的。

sentences.en: Despite her suspicions, Julia was at a loss as to why her neighbour would have broken into her house and taken a knife to her things.
sentences.zh: 尽管有怀疑，朱莉娅还是不明白为什么她的邻居会闯入她的房子并用刀破坏她的东西。

sentences.en: I hadn't done anything.
sentences.zh: 我什么都没做。

sentences.en: I'd been only ever hospitable and welcoming.
sentences.zh: 我一直都很好客、很友善。

sentences.en: It is an odd thing for any person to have done, to have behaved in that way.
sentences.zh: 对任何人来说，做出这种行为都是一件奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: I don't think there's a thing that I did that could have caused it or have changed it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我做了什么会导致或改变这种结果的事。

sentences.en: While the uniformed members that Julia reported to at the Frankston police didn't seem to focus on Denya as a suspect in her break-in,
sentences.zh: 虽然朱莉娅向弗兰克斯顿警方报告时，制服警员似乎并没有把丹耶作为入室行窃的嫌疑人，

sentences.en: he had certainly come onto the radar with the local CIB detectives.
sentences.zh: 但他确实已经进入了当地刑事调查局侦探的视线。

sentences.en: Veteran detective Cole Clark had an encounter with Denya he never forgot.
sentences.zh: 资深侦探科尔·克拉克曾与丹耶有过一次他永生难忘的遭遇。

sentences.en: Maybe 12 months, two years prior to him committing these murders, I remember I was working an afternoon shift in Frankston and I was called to Langwarrand, a shopping centre,
sentences.zh: 在他犯下这些谋杀案的大约12个月或两年前，我记得我在弗兰克斯顿上晚班，接到电话去朗沃伦的一个购物中心，

sentences.en: and where the uniformed blokes had been called by one of the shopkeepers that someone had been seen bleeding outside one of the shops and had taken off.
sentences.zh: 制服警员接到店主报警，说有人在店外流血，然后逃跑了。

sentences.en: It turned and we found a blood trail that led from the shops down a couple of the streets and along the footpaths, but it then disappeared.
sentences.zh: 我们发现了一条血迹，从商店一直延伸到几条街道和人行道上，但随后消失了。

sentences.en: I remember that we then got a phone call while we were investigating this that a male person had been admitted to Frankston Hospital, I think it was,
sentences.zh: 我记得我们在调查时接到电话，说一名男性被送进了弗兰克斯顿医院，我想是这样，

sentences.en: with a stab wound to his leg, upper leg, I think, from memory.
sentences.zh: 腿部有刺伤，大腿，我记得是这样。

sentences.en: We went to the hospital, tried to speak to the person that was involved and it turns out that it was Paul Denier at the time,
sentences.zh: 我们去了医院，试图与相关人员交谈，结果发现当时就是保罗·丹耶，

sentences.en: had suffered a leg wound and was being stitched up in hospital
sentences.zh: 他腿部受伤，正在医院缝针。

sentences.en: We tried to speak to him.
sentences.zh: 我们试图和他谈谈。

sentences.en: He remained mute at the time and wouldn't tell us how he got the wound or where he got the wound or the circumstances and how it happened.
sentences.zh: 他当时保持沉默，不肯告诉我们他是怎么受伤的，在哪里受伤的，或者受伤的情况和经过。

sentences.en: In hindsight, years later when he started killing people and he admitted that he was running around cutting the throats of animals around Langwarren at the time,
sentences.zh: 事后看来，多年后当他开始杀人并承认当时他在朗沃伦到处割动物喉咙时，

sentences.en: I surmised later on that while he was trying to kill an animal, he'd actually stabbed himself in the leg.
sentences.zh: 我后来推测，他在试图杀死动物时，实际上刺伤了自己的腿。

sentences.en: And, of course, he wouldn't assist us in any way as to what had happened.
sentences.zh: 当然，他拒绝以任何方式协助我们说明发生了什么。

sentences.en: So we couldn't take the matter any further.
sentences.zh: 所以我们无法进一步处理此事。

sentences.en: He signed a statement.
sentences.zh: 他签署了一份声明。

sentences.en: He wanted no further action involving the police in relation to this matter.
sentences.zh: 他要求不再采取涉及警方的行动。

sentences.en: So we made inquiries the next day around the area if anybody had lost animals or had anything killed.
sentences.zh: 所以第二天我们在该地区进行了询问，看是否有人丢失了动物或有动物被杀。

sentences.en: Nothing came forward.
sentences.zh: 一无所获。

sentences.en: And I remember speaking to one of the brothers that night, trying to get the brother to find out what had happened from him
sentences.zh: 我记得那天晚上和他的一个兄弟谈过，试图让兄弟从他那里打听发生了什么，

sentences.en: and the brother said he wouldn't even talk to me about it.
sentences.zh: 但他兄弟说他甚至不愿和我谈论这件事。

sentences.en: So, yeah, you look back in reality on that and you say, well, he obviously had problems in those times and this was early in the piece,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，当你回顾现实时，你会说，他当时显然有问题，而且这还是早期阶段，

sentences.en: which he admitted to later on that he'd been doing it.
sentences.zh: 他后来承认他当时确实在做这些事。

sentences.en: Gee, you sit there and think, well, maybe if we had oppressed it further or whatever and got into his mind, we may have stopped these murders, but I seriously doubt it.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你坐在那儿想，好吧，也许如果我们进一步施压或者什么的，进入他的内心，我们可能阻止这些谋杀，但我严重怀疑这一点。

sentences.en: but it's sort of things run through your mind.
sentences.zh: 但这些事情确实会在你脑海中闪过。

sentences.en: These encounters with Paul Denyer certainly left their mark on police and civilians alike.
sentences.zh: 这些与保罗·丹耶的遭遇确实给警察和平民都留下了深刻的印记。

sentences.en: Once Julia moved out, Paul Denyer took his coffee visits down to the next unit where Trisha Vaines lived and her sister Donna occasionally stayed.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅搬走后，保罗·丹耶把他的“咖啡拜访”转移到了隔壁特里莎·维恩斯住的公寓，她的妹妹唐娜偶尔也会住在那儿。

sentences.en: Sadly, Donna passed away in 2018 but her mother, Gloria Vaines, wanted to tell Donna's story.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，唐娜于2018年去世了，但她的母亲格洛丽亚·维恩斯想讲述唐娜的故事。

sentences.en: She moved into Franks and Dandenong Road, yes, into, it was a big block of units and he was in the front one with his fiancée.
sentences.zh: 她搬进了弗兰克斯顿的丹德农路，是的，那是一个很大的公寓区，他和他未婚妻住在最前面那一间。

sentences.en: Very nice guy, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实是个很好的人。

sentences.en: Very nice guy, very neighbourly.
sentences.zh: 非常好的人，很有邻里情谊。

sentences.en: Would do anything for you.
sentences.zh: 愿意为你做任何事。

sentences.en: Always said hello when he saw me when I went to visit Patricia.
sentences.zh: 我去看望帕特里夏时，他见到我总是会打招呼。

sentences.en: He had been in at Trisha's for a coffee, I think mainly after Donna moved in there.
sentences.zh: 我想他去特里莎那儿喝咖啡，主要是唐娜搬进去之后。

sentences.en: She went to stay with her sister for a while and he did go there for coffee.
sentences.zh: 她去她姐姐那儿住了一段时间，他确实去那儿喝过咖啡。

sentences.en: I asked Gloria for her impressions of Paul Denyer.
sentences.zh: 我问格洛丽亚对保罗·丹耶的印象。

sentences.en: He always said hi to me in the driveway, a big smile.
sentences.zh: 他在车道上见到我总是会打招呼，笑得很灿烂。

sentences.en: He just seemed like one of a big, chubby, happy-go-lucky bloke.
sentences.zh: 他看起来就像个胖乎乎、乐天派的家伙。

sentences.en: Never would have picked him otherwise for him, you know, just a nice neighbour.
sentences.zh: 否则你绝不会那样看他，你知道，他只是个好邻居。

sentences.en: In late January 1993, Donna and her partner Les rented their own place in Claude Street, not far from her sister's unit.
sentences.zh: 1993年1月底，唐娜和她的伴侣莱斯在克劳德街租了自己的房子，离她姐姐的公寓不远。

sentences.en: Then she moved into the street behind Tricia, it was roughly behind the next street down or something, into a unit with her partner Les at the time.
sentences.zh: 然后她搬到了特里莎后面的那条街，大概是后面那条街之类的，和当时的伴侣莱斯住进了一间公寓。

sentences.en: Donna, Les and their baby daughter had lived in the unit in Claude Street for just three weeks when Paul Denyer broke in and changed the course of Donna's life.
sentences.zh: 唐娜、莱斯和他们的小女儿在克劳德街的公寓里才住了三周，保罗·丹耶就闯了进来，改变了唐娜的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: In what was always regarded from a distance as a lucky break, on the night Denya broke in, Donna wasn't home.
sentences.zh: 在丹雅闯入的那晚，唐娜恰好不在家，这在当时看来一直被认为是一次幸运的巧合。

sentences.en: Les worked during the day at his regular job and at night he would supplement the family income by delivering pizzas.
sentences.zh: 莱斯白天有一份正职，晚上则通过送外卖来补贴家用。

sentences.en: Donna often went out with Les on his pizza delivery, but on the night of Friday the 19th of February, she said she would just stay home and bath the baby.
sentences.zh: 唐娜经常陪莱斯一起去送外卖，但在2月19日那个周五的晚上，她说她想待在家里给孩子洗澡。

sentences.en: Donna got bored very, very easily, always bored, and she always went with him.
sentences.zh: 唐娜很容易感到无聊，总是觉得闷，所以她通常都会跟着他。

sentences.en: She used to go everywhere, and he was surprised at that, and now she said, no, are you sure?
sentences.zh: 她以前去哪儿都跟着，所以莱斯对此感到惊讶，而这次她说不去了，他还问她确定吗？

sentences.en: You'll be bored.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得无聊的。

sentences.en: She said, no, can't be bothered.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，我懒得动。

sentences.en: She'll just bath the baby.
sentences.zh: 她只想给孩子洗个澡。

sentences.en: Donna bathed the baby and left the water in the tub.
sentences.zh: 唐娜给孩子洗完澡后，把水留在了浴缸里。

sentences.en: The night dragged on, and she was pleased when Les dropped back home in the middle of his shift.
sentences.zh: 夜晚漫长，当莱斯在送餐间隙顺路回家时，她感到很高兴。

sentences.en: Anyway, she must have been thinking, and I wished I'd gone, I wished I'd gone.
sentences.zh: 总之，她当时一定在想，真希望我跟着去了，真希望我跟着去了。

sentences.en: He came back, he was on the way to deliver a pizza and he called in and they said, are you bored yet, do you want to come?
sentences.zh: 他回来时正要去送下一单，他顺道过来问她，现在无聊了吗，想一起去吗？

sentences.en: She said, oh yes.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，想去。

sentences.en: So she dried the baby, put her in the car and off they went.
sentences.zh: 于是她擦干孩子，把她放进车里，他们就出发了。

sentences.en: I think it was about 8.30ish or something.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是八点半左右吧。

sentences.en: And then I think when they got back, I think it was 11.30 for some of us around then.
sentences.zh: 后来我想他们回来的时候，大概是十一点半左右，我们有些人当时就在那儿。

sentences.en: What Donna and Les found when they returned home was something so cruel and violent,
sentences.zh: 唐娜和莱斯回到家时，眼前的一幕极其残忍和暴力，

sentences.en: It was beyond belief.
sentences.zh: 简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: At first she didn't go into the unit because she was getting the baby out the capsule in the car and Les went to open the front door.
sentences.zh: 起初她没有进屋，因为她正在车里把孩子从提篮里抱出来，莱斯则去开前门。

sentences.en: And he had called her.
sentences.zh: 他当时叫了她一声。

sentences.en: I think she said she heard him saying, oh my God, or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我想她说她听到他喊了声“天哪”之类的。

sentences.en: A bit of a shock response.
sentences.zh: 这是一种受到惊吓后的反应。

sentences.en: And he said to her, Donna, don't come in.
sentences.zh: 他对她说，唐娜，别进来。

sentences.en: The reason Les didn't want Donna to come in was because he had seen the place had been broken into.
sentences.zh: 莱斯不让唐娜进屋的原因是他发现家里被人闯入了。

sentences.en: Like Julia's break-in months earlier, nothing had been taken.
sentences.zh: 就像几个月前朱莉家被闯入时一样，家里什么东西都没丢。

sentences.en: The intruder had just left carnage in their wake.
sentences.zh: 入侵者只是在他们家里留下了一片狼藉。

sentences.en: When Les opened the front door, there was an overwhelming smell and he discovered their cat horribly slaughtered on the floor in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 当莱斯打开前门时，一股刺鼻的气味扑面而来，他发现他们的猫被残忍地屠杀在厨房地板上。

sentences.en: Someone had written Donna You're Dead and the name Robin on the wall in what looked like cat's blood.
sentences.zh: 有人用看起来像是猫血的东西在墙上写下了“唐娜，你死定了”以及“罗宾”这个名字。

sentences.en: The names in blood meant it wasn't a random break-in.
sentences.zh: 用血写下的名字意味着这绝非随机的入室行窃。

sentences.en: Donna assumed the reference was to her dad, who was Rob, but sometimes called Robin.
sentences.zh: 唐娜以为这是指她的父亲，他叫罗伯，但有时也被称为罗宾。

sentences.en: After calling the police, Gloria was the next to get a call.
sentences.zh: 在报警之后，格洛丽亚是下一个接到电话的人。

sentences.en: Donna rang and I was shocked, but I'd have been more shocked if I knew the reason her place had been broken into, because then it was just her place had been broken into.
sentences.zh: 唐娜打来电话，我当时很震惊，但如果我知道她家被闯入的原因，我会更震惊，因为当时我只以为那是普通的入室行窃。

sentences.en: We didn't know who it was and the cats, and I thought, God, who would do that?
sentences.zh: 我们不知道是谁干的，还有那些猫，我心想，天哪，谁会做出这种事？

sentences.en: So we were a bit sort of, why, who would do that?
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时有点困惑，为什么，谁会做这种事？

sentences.en: And obviously somebody knew them because the names were on the wall so they knew who lived there.
sentences.zh: 显然有人认识他们，因为墙上写着名字，所以他们知道谁住在那儿。

sentences.en: Well, Donna didn't and her dad was Rob, Robin, whichever.
sentences.zh: 嗯，唐娜不知道，她父亲叫罗伯，或者罗宾，随你怎么叫吧。

sentences.en: I said, well, look, do you want to come here, grab some clothes?
sentences.zh: 我说，你看，你要不要过来我这儿，拿点衣服？

sentences.en: And she said, no, not at the moment, the police are here.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，现在不用了，警察在这儿。

sentences.en: One of the police called to the break-in at Donna's flat was Chris McCann from the newly formed police special response squad
sentences.zh: 负责唐娜公寓入室行窃案的警察之一是克里斯·麦肯，他来自新成立的警察特别响应小组。

sentences.en: The squad was a brand new iteration of the Major Crime Squad and had been very busy in their first two months of operation.
sentences.zh: 该小组是重案组的一个全新迭代版本，在成立的前两个月里非常忙碌。

sentences.en: Chris himself had arrested nearly 50 people in that time.
sentences.zh: 克里斯本人在那段时间里逮捕了近50人。

sentences.en: So our squad was the Special Response Squad, which had been formed as a result of the disbanding of what was called the Major Crime Squad in those days.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的小组是特别响应小组，它是由于当时所谓的重案组解散而成立的。

sentences.en: Primarily, we were established to investigate aggravated burglaries, so armed robberies on homes.
sentences.zh: 我们成立的主要目的是调查加重入室盗窃案，也就是针对住宅的武装抢劫。

sentences.en: Any break-in where there was any suggestion or evidence of a weapon being used, we would be called out to that job.
sentences.zh: 任何有迹象或证据表明使用了武器的入室行窃，我们都会被派去处理。

sentences.en: And I think at the time, we'd only been operating for,
sentences.zh: 我想当时我们才刚开始运作，

sentences.en: I'm going to say, two months.
sentences.zh: 我想大概有两个月吧。

sentences.en: In the early hours of the morning of Saturday 20th February,
sentences.zh: 在2月20日星期六的凌晨，

sentences.en: Chris McCann arrived at Donna's place in Claude Street.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·麦肯到达了位于克劳德街的唐娜家。

sentences.en: We were called out early in the morning and I went there with my crew and we met up with the Frankston detectives.
sentences.zh: 我们一大早就接到了出警通知，我和我的队员去了那里，并与弗兰克斯顿的侦探们会合。

sentences.en: And it was just a brown brick unit in the middle of Frankston.
sentences.zh: 那只是弗兰克斯顿中心地带的一栋棕色砖房公寓。

sentences.en: And when we went to the scene, I do recall that there was like a bucket that was underneath the rear window.
sentences.zh: 当我们到达现场时，我记得后窗下面有个桶。

sentences.en: When we called the crime scene forensics out and photographs,
sentences.zh: 当我们叫来犯罪现场取证人员进行拍照时，

sentences.en: There was blood marks or blood stains from gloves that you could clearly see on the roll-down blinds.
sentences.zh: 在卷帘上可以清楚地看到手套留下的血迹或血渍。

sentences.en: And afterwards, when the forensic guys used their inhydrin and the ultraviolet light, they picked up one stone boot impressions all across the kitchen floor and in the laundry.
sentences.zh: 事后，当法医使用茚三酮和紫外线灯时，他们在整个厨房地板和洗衣房里发现了鞋印。

sentences.en: Even though 30 years have gone by since the job in Claude Street,
sentences.zh: 尽管克劳德街的案子已经过去30年了，

sentences.en: Chris has never forgotten the site that he was met with when he walked into the flat.
sentences.zh: 克里斯永远不会忘记他走进公寓时所看到的景象。

sentences.en: One of the Frankston detectives pre-warned him before he went inside.
sentences.zh: 其中一名弗兰克斯顿的侦探在他进去之前预先警告了他。

sentences.en: Here's what the scene looked like, and be aware, this is distressing.
sentences.zh: 这就是现场的样子，请注意，这会让人感到不安。

sentences.en: After you were told that somebody had been in there and had gone on a rampage with a knife, he said, you need to be prepared because it's a mess in there.
sentences.zh: 在被告知有人闯入并持刀疯狂破坏后，他说，你需要做好心理准备，因为里面一团糟。

sentences.en: He's killed some cats and some kittens.
sentences.zh: 他杀了一些猫和幼猫。

sentences.en: and so as you walk through the front door, you're immediately hit with this horrible stench and then really the horrible image of seeing a female cat
sentences.zh: 所以当你走进前门时，立刻就会闻到那股可怕的恶臭，然后是看到一只母猫的恐怖景象，

sentences.en: that had been completely gutted and at that time on the walls, as you walk in through the door, there were death threats written on the wall using the intestines of the cat
sentences.zh: 它被彻底开膛破肚了，当时在墙上，当你走进门时，墙上用猫的内脏写着死亡威胁，

sentences.en: and then in the bathroom there was kittens that had their throats cut and they had been then thrown into the bath.
sentences.zh: 然后在浴室里，有几只幼猫被割断了喉咙，然后被扔进了浴缸里。

sentences.en: And then as you move through the unit, I remember seeing a half-naked picture of a woman attached to the cat with stab marks that had gone through the picture into the cat
sentences.zh: 接着当你穿过公寓时，我记得看到一张半裸女人的照片贴在猫身上，刀痕穿过照片刺进了猫的身体，

sentences.en: and then there was a bassinet in the main bedroom and in the bassinet there were more pictures of half-dressed women with stab marks through the pictures into the bassinet
sentences.zh: 主卧里还有一个摇篮，摇篮里有更多半裸女人的照片，刀痕穿过照片刺进了摇篮里，

sentences.en: and then behind one of the cupboard doors there had obviously been some pictures there and there had been slash marks from a knife
sentences.zh: 然后在一个橱柜门后面，显然也贴过一些照片，上面有刀割的痕迹，

sentences.en: obviously where then you had slashed through the photographs and the pictures on the back of the door.
sentences.zh: 显然是有人用刀划破了门后的照片和图片。

sentences.en: in the lounge room was an orange baby bouncer sitting in the middle of the floor on a pink
sentences.zh: 在客厅里，一个橙色的婴儿摇椅放在地板中央，铺在一条粉色

sentences.en: and blue checkered rug next to it lay a baby's rattle and a disposable nappy on the white wall
sentences.zh: 和蓝色格子地毯上，旁边放着一个婴儿拨浪鼓和一片一次性尿布，在白色的墙上，

sentences.en: of the lounge room next to the television the intruder had written what looked like dead don
sentences.zh: 客厅电视机旁边，入侵者写下了看起来像是“死唐”的字样，

sentences.en: in a red substance that looked like blood in the kitchen written in blood above the stove were the words Donner You're Dead printed in block letters.
sentences.zh: 用的是一种看起来像血的红色物质，在厨房炉灶上方用血写着“唐娜，你死定了”，用的是印刷体大写字母。

sentences.en: Next to the words was a bloodied outline to suggest that the cat had either been held or flung against the wall.
sentences.zh: 在字迹旁边有一个血迹斑斑的轮廓，暗示猫要么是被按住，要么是被甩在了墙上。

sentences.en: Among the wall writings was the name Robin.
sentences.zh: 墙上的字迹中还包括“罗宾”这个名字。

sentences.en: In the bathroom were the two kittens, floating one at each end of a half-filled bath.
sentences.zh: 浴室里有两只幼猫，漂浮在半满的浴缸两端。

sentences.en: They had turned the water rust-coloured with their blood.
sentences.zh: 它们的血把水染成了铁锈色。

sentences.en: The attack on the kittens had occurred in the laundry over a plastic laundry basket of baby clothes.
sentences.zh: 对小猫的袭击发生在洗衣房里，就在一个装满婴儿衣服的塑料洗衣篮上。

sentences.en: Blood had splashed everywhere, spraying high up the walls and around a packet of kitty litter.
sentences.zh: 血迹溅得到处都是，高高地喷溅在墙上，还溅到了猫砂袋周围。

sentences.en: In the cat's blood on the floor was a distinct shoe impression.
sentences.zh: 地板上猫的血迹中留下了一个清晰的鞋印。

sentences.en: In the main bedroom, the intruder had ransacked the cupboards and drawers and sprayed a can of shaving cream all over Donna's mirror and through the creamy swirls,
sentences.zh: 在主卧里，闯入者翻乱了橱柜和抽屉，还在唐娜的镜子上喷满了剃须膏，透过那奶油般的漩涡，

sentences.en: the detectives could make out the words Donna and Robin.
sentences.zh: 侦探们辨认出了“唐娜”和“罗宾”这两个字。

sentences.en: One of the cupboard doors had been covered in pictures of swimsuit models.
sentences.zh: 其中一个橱柜门上贴满了泳装模特的照片。

sentences.en: These had been slashed and only a few jagged corners of the pictures remained.
sentences.zh: 这些照片被划破了，只剩下几个参差不齐的边角。

sentences.en: The intruder had also slashed the cupboard door, leaving deep gouges in the wood.
sentences.zh: 闯入者还划破了橱柜门，在木头上留下了深深的刻痕。

sentences.en: Oddly the door had swirls of dirty dried water marks as if the attacker had wanted to clean the surface for some reason.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，门上还有一圈圈脏兮兮的干涸水渍，仿佛袭击者出于某种原因想把表面擦干净。

sentences.en: Had he written another message on it then changed his mind?
sentences.zh: 难道他在上面写了另一条信息，然后又改变主意了？

sentences.en: Outside the point of entry was clear.
sentences.zh: 外面的入口点很明显。

sentences.en: The intruder had climbed onto a nappy bucket around the back, forced a window open and climbed through.
sentences.zh: 闯入者爬上了后院的一个尿布桶，撬开窗户钻了进去。

sentences.en: Left behind on the blind was a gloved hand impression in blood.
sentences.zh: 百叶窗上留下了一个带血的手套手印。

sentences.en: For Detective Chris McCann, the scene was like nothing he'd ever seen before.
sentences.zh: 对于克里斯·麦肯侦探来说，眼前的景象是他从未见过的。

sentences.en: Police officers see the worst of the worst, but there was something about the break-in at Donna's house that stood out for Chris.
sentences.zh: 警察见惯了最糟糕的罪案，但唐娜家发生的这起入室盗窃案对克里斯来说有些不同寻常。

sentences.en: I'd been to numerous homicides and I'd been to numerous violent crimes,
sentences.zh: 我处理过无数起凶杀案，也去过无数次暴力犯罪现场，

sentences.en: but this was particularly different because of the violent nature in which he had just slaughtered the defenseless animals.
sentences.zh: 但这起案件特别不同，因为他屠杀那些手无寸铁的动物时所表现出的暴力性质。

sentences.en: And you wouldn't see that normally unless it was a frenzied attack by an ex-boyfriend on a girlfriend, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，除非是前男友对女友发起的疯狂袭击，否则你不会看到这种场面。

sentences.en: But when you saw it, it seemed to be completely out of place with a normal break-in at a house.
sentences.zh: 但当你看到它时，它似乎与普通的入室盗窃完全不搭界。

sentences.en: If they were breaking into steel or something, you would normally then go on a rampage and kill the animals in the house and then write death threats.
sentences.zh: 如果他们是为了入室抢劫或类似目的，通常不会接着大肆破坏、杀害家里的动物，然后还写下死亡威胁。

sentences.en: So, no, I'd never seen anything like that before.
sentences.zh: 所以，不，我以前从未见过这样的事。

sentences.en: Forensic psychologist Tim Watson-Monroe offers his insights.
sentences.zh: 法医心理学家蒂姆·沃森-门罗提出了他的见解。

sentences.en: The way you describe that crime scene, the disembowelling of the cats, naked women.
sentences.zh: 你描述的那个犯罪现场，猫被开膛破肚，还有裸体女性的照片。

sentences.en: Now, some would say perhaps this is the indicators of a person with a psychotic mind, somebody that's out of touch with reality.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人可能会说这或许是一个精神病患者的迹象，一个与现实脱节的人。

sentences.en: Because I think probably the layperson, that's crazy behaviour, and it is.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为普通人会觉得这是疯狂的行为，事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: But it's not medically defined or legally defined insanity.
sentences.zh: 但这在医学或法律上并不属于精神错乱的定义。

sentences.en: He clearly knew what he was doing.
sentences.zh: 他很清楚自己在做什么。

sentences.en: His focus was really to not only act out on that fantasy, but create fear, vicarious power, vicarious control.
sentences.zh: 他的重点不仅是付诸实施那种幻想，更是为了制造恐惧，获得代理权力和代理控制感。

sentences.en: And it's all planned and premeditated.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是经过策划和预谋的。

sentences.en: It's not shambolic thinking in the way that you normally get with psychotic people.
sentences.zh: 这不像精神病患者通常表现出的那种混乱思维。

sentences.en: One of the reasons Chris still remembers the case, aside from the violence, is perhaps because Donna and Les had a newborn baby.
sentences.zh: 除了暴力程度外，克里斯至今仍记得这个案子的原因之一，或许是因为唐娜和莱斯当时有一个刚出生的婴儿。

sentences.en: Gloria Vaines remembers Donna and Les taking the baby and leaving the scene to the police.
sentences.zh: 格洛丽亚·维恩斯记得唐娜和莱斯带着孩子离开了现场，交由警方处理。

sentences.en: He went to stay with Les's mum.
sentences.zh: 他去莱斯的母亲家住了。

sentences.en: She lived in Frankston as well.
sentences.zh: 她也住在弗兰克斯顿。

sentences.en: Donna needed Gloria's help.
sentences.zh: 唐娜需要格洛丽亚的帮助。

sentences.en: Once the crime scene was processed, the cats needed to be transported for post-mortem examination and the police apparently didn't do the transportation.
sentences.zh: 犯罪现场处理完毕后，猫的尸体需要被送去进行尸检，而警方显然没有负责运输。

sentences.en: When I got there, it was just a madhouse of police vehicles and lights.
sentences.zh: 当我到达那里时，到处都是警车和警灯，简直乱成了一锅粥。

sentences.en: Gloria brought a friend with her.
sentences.zh: 格洛丽亚带了一个朋友一起来。

sentences.en: Gloria's friend Sandy was a vet nurse and on the way the two had stopped off at a local vet to try and procure body bags for the cats
sentences.zh: 格洛丽亚的朋友桑迪是一名兽医护士，在路上两人顺道去了一家当地的兽医诊所，试图为猫弄到尸体袋，

sentences.en: which were essentially black plastic garbage bags.
sentences.zh: 那其实就是黑色塑料垃圾袋。

sentences.en: When Gloria began telling me about collecting the cats her own cat came into the room and started meowing.
sentences.zh: 当格洛丽亚开始向我讲述收集猫尸体的事时，她自己的猫走进房间开始喵喵叫。

sentences.en: It was a bit haunting to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这让人感到有点毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: we got to the house and the police she said don't you come in i said not coming in i stayed in the
sentences.zh: 我们到了那所房子，警察说“别进来”，我说“我不进去”，我就待在

sentences.en: car oh there was reporters and god knows what going on she went in she came out with them in the bag
sentences.zh: 车里。哦，到处都是记者，天知道发生了什么。她进去了，出来时带着装猫的袋子，

sentences.en: put them in the boot and she said they're hopeless the police are hopeless she said they had them in
sentences.zh: 把它们放进后备箱。她说：“他们太无能了，警察太无能了。”她说他们把猫装在

sentences.en: a clear plastic bag she said the metal it was horrible she said they could have put them in something else.
sentences.zh: 一个透明塑料袋里，她说那场面太可怕了，她说他们本可以把它们装在别的东西里。

sentences.en: So she put that into the black bag.
sentences.zh: 所以她把那个袋子放进了黑色的袋子里。

sentences.en: And we had to go all the way to Surrey Hills.
sentences.zh: 然后我们不得不一路赶往萨里山。

sentences.en: Apparently that's where the police would take it there.
sentences.zh: 显然警察就是把尸体送到那里去的。

sentences.en: That's the veterinary pathologiSt.
sentences.zh: 那是兽医病理学家所在的地方。

sentences.en: And they can tell what the blade size or whatever, the type of knife that may have been used or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们能判断出刀刃的大小，或者可能使用了什么类型的刀之类的。

sentences.en: So we trotted off to Surrey Hills that night.
sentences.zh: 所以那天晚上我们匆匆赶往萨里山。

sentences.en: Leaving Donna's flat with the murdered cats in her boot, Gloria and her friend ran the gauntlet of the press.
sentences.zh: 格洛丽亚和她的朋友带着后备箱里被杀害的猫，离开了唐娜的公寓，冲破了媒体的围堵。

sentences.en: When we left with my friend and I to take the cats' bodies to the pathologist so we came out the driver, you know, they're up against the car with their cameras and the reporters.
sentences.zh: 当我们和我的朋友离开去把猫的尸体送给病理学家时，我们出来，司机，你知道的，他们拿着摄像机和麦克风围在车边。

sentences.en: After Chris
sentences.zh: 在克里斯·

sentences.en: McCann and his crew had finished examining the scene, they went around to Les's mum to interview the young couple.
sentences.zh: 麦肯和他的团队完成现场勘查后，他们去了莱斯的母亲家采访这对年轻夫妇。

sentences.en: It's hard to imagine anyone hating a young woman with a baby so much they would commit such a violent act on her cat and kittens.
sentences.zh: 很难想象有人会如此憎恨一个带着婴儿的年轻女子，以至于会对她的猫和幼崽做出如此暴力的行为。

sentences.en: The detectives were in no doubt that had Donna and her baby been home when the intruder broke in, they too would have been murdered.
sentences.zh: 侦探们毫不怀疑，如果闯入者破门而入时唐娜和她的孩子在家，她们也会被杀害。

sentences.en: Because it was so unusual what had happened, we had asked them, because generally with something like this, this is almost like a crime of hate
sentences.zh: 因为发生的事情太不寻常了，我们询问了他们，因为通常像这样的事情，这几乎就像是一种仇恨犯罪，

sentences.en: that you either hate the actual human or you hate animals or both.
sentences.zh: 要么你憎恨那个具体的人，要么你憎恨动物，或者两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: And so we wanted to get an understanding about who they thought may have had some sort of vendetta against them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想了解一下他们认为谁可能对他们怀有某种宿怨。

sentences.en: But these are young kids without any history of criminal involvement.
sentences.zh: 但他们只是没有犯罪前科的年轻人。

sentences.en: So it wasn't something, they were unable to come up with names and they eventually gave us a list of about 10 people in there.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是什么……他们无法提供具体的名字，最终给了我们一份大约10人的名单。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if in that list Paul Denier's name had been mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我不确定那份名单里是否提到了保罗·丹尼尔的名字。

sentences.en: I remember afterwards she said that there was somebody strange at a place that she had visited.
sentences.zh: 我记得后来她说，在她去过的一个地方遇到过一个奇怪的人。

sentences.en: It was either her sister or her friend lived in Frankston
sentences.zh: 要么是她姐姐，要么是她朋友住在弗兰克斯顿，

sentences.en: and that turned out to be Paul Denier.
